guild.about: Two narrow specialists that hand off through a queue table.

roles.focus: Find new candidates and write them to the queue.

task.body:
Start of work: read Memory, then note_get agent/scout/playbook.md and apply it.

Before queueing a candidate, check seen-set with record_list where key is the candidate name in lower case. Add each new candidate to scout-queue with record_add (name, source_url, status new), then record_add its key and source to seen-set. The runtime assigns ids; never send one. The archivist drains scout-queue; do not archive. When a sweep shows what separates a real candidate from noise, revise the playbook with note_write.

schedules.instruction: Sweep for new candidates. Skip keys already in seen-set (record_list where key); add the rest to scout-queue with status new.

roles.focus: Read the queue and write the durable record.

task.body:
Start of work: read Memory. The map below says which Notion property each scout-queue column lands in.

![[agent/archivist/notion-map.md]]

Find scout-queue records with record_list where status new and archive each one, then record_update that record by id with status archived, or rejected with a reason. The scout fills scout-queue; do not scout.

schedules.instruction: Archive scout-queue records whose status is new; record_update each one to status archived when done.

collections.name: scout-queue
collections.purpose: One record per candidate: the scout adds it, the archivist drains it and sets the outcome.

columns.name: status
columns.description: new when the scout adds it; the archivist sets archived or rejected

collections.name: seen-set
collections.purpose: One record per candidate key the scout has already queued, so a sweep never re-queues it.

columns.name: source
columns.description: Where the candidate was first seen

columns.name: first_seen
columns.description: When the sweep that recorded it ran

notes.body: What a real candidate looks like versus noise. The scout revises it as it learns.
Which Notion database property each scout-queue column lands in. The operator edits it; the archivist reads it every wake.

connections.hint: Live web results for the scout.
connections.setup: Nothing to connect while the platform's web search is on; otherwise add a Tavily API key on the organisation.
Connect Notion on the organisation and confirm the destination database. Queues stay in local collections.

resources.title: Archive
resources.use: Long-lived archived candidates. Not the scout queue.

systems.name: web-search
systems.reason: Scouting needs live web results; the web search connector serves them.

systems.name: notion
systems.reason: Durable archive the operator already owns.

specialization.detail: Owns the candidate playbook it revises; needs web search, never Notion.
Owns Notion page creation and the archive map; needs no web search.
